t: Pinpointing and Rolling Back Specific Files with Git: A Jekyll Case Study
s: This article details using Git to selectively revert problematic template changes in a Jekyll site that caused a traffic drop, while preserving new content. It explores Git commands for identifying and isolating modified and added files between commits to restore functionality without data loss.
sub: Git branching for experimentation and safety
Identifying specific file changes (added/modified) using git diff
Selective file reversion in Git while preserving new content
Troubleshooting website performance drops with Git version control
